'''Michael''' "'''Mike'''" '''Shulman''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|uː|l|m|ə|n}}; born 1980) is an American professor of mathematics at the [[University of San Diego]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Shulman, PhD |website=University of San Diego |url=https://www.sandiego.edu/directory/biography.php?profile_id=682 |access-date=March 24, 2021}}</ref> who works in [[category theory]] and [[higher category theory]], [[homotopy theory]], [[Mathematical logic|logic as applied to set theory]], and [[computer science]].

==Work==
Shulman did his undergraduate work at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and his postgraduate work at the [[University of Cambridge]] and the [[University of Chicago]], where he received his Ph.D. in 2009.

His doctoral thesis and subsequent work dealt with applications of category theory to homotopy theory.

In 2009, he received a [[National Science Foundation]] Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowship.<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/michael-shulman Michael Shulman] page at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] School of Mathematics</ref>

In 2012–13, he was a visiting scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/mshulman |website=Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars |title=Michael Shulman}}</ref> where he was one of the official participants in the ''Special Year on Univalent Foundations of Mathematics''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.math.ias.edu/sp/univalent/participants |title=IAS Program Participants Members |website= IAS school of mathematics: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics|date=13 July 2012 }}</ref> Shulman was one of the principal authors of the book ''Homotopy type theory: Univalent foundations of mathematics'',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://github.com/HoTT/book/graphs/contributors |title=HoTT/book Contributions to master, excluding merge commits |website=GitHub}}</ref> an informal exposition on the basics of [[univalent foundations]] and [[homotopy type theory]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/2013/06/the_hott_book.html |website=The n-Category Café |title=The HoTT Book |first=Mike |last=Shulman |date=20 June 2013}}</ref> In 2014, Shulman was part of a team headed by [[Steve Awodey]] that was awarded a $7.5M grant from the [[Air Force Research Laboratory]] for homotopy type theory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2014/april/april28_awodeygrant.html |website=Carnegie Mellon University |title=Press Release: Carnegie Mellon Awarded $7.5 Million Department of Defense Grant To Reshape Mathematics |date=28 April 2014}}</ref>

==Social views==

Shulman is a [[Social conservatism|social conservative]], opposing the idea that [[Social construction of gender|gender is socially constructed]] and the use of [[singular they]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=HoTT |title=Use inclusive language in §1.11 by ThePuzzlemaker · Pull Request #1101 · HoTT/book |url=https://github.com/HoTT/book/pull/1101 |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=GitHub |language=en}}</ref> In April 2022, organizers of the Homotopy Type Theory Electronic Seminar Talks canceled a distinguished lecture series to be given by Shulman due to statements he made being in conflict with the organization's commitment to diversity in the mathematics community.<ref>{{Cite web |title=M. Shulman, Towards Third-Generation HOTT, April 14, 21, and 28 - HoTTEST Distinguished Lecture Series |url=https://groups.google.com/g/homotopytypetheory/c/L53FHA2gDGI/m/7TTK96UCAgAJ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=groups.google.com}}</ref>

==Blogs==
Shulman is a supporter of using web-based software systems, such as [[GitHub]], to promote collaborative work by mathematicians—the six-hundred-page ''Homotopy type theory'' book being a notable example. He is a prolific contributor to the [[nLab|''n''Lab]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ncatlab.org/nlab/authors?page=4 |title=nLab Authors }}</ref> (and a member of its steering committee<ref>[http://ncatlab.org/nlabmeta/show/steering+committee nLab: steering committee]</ref>), and a co-host of the homotopy type theory blog<ref>[http://homotopytypetheory.org/blog Homotopy type theory blog]</ref> and of the [[John C. Baez#Blogs|''n''-Category Cafe]], a blog focusing on higher category theory,<ref>[https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/shulman.html Shulman postings to ''n''-Category Cafe blog]</ref> as well as a blog about Narya proof assistant.<ref>[https://gwaithimirdain.github.io/blog/ Gwaith-i-Mírdain Development Blog]</ref>
